even-pairs.computes: first symbol equals last symbol (5-state WFSA)
even-pairs.structural_note: Binary alphabet, no marker/shape distinct from the semantic rule itself; the accept condition is a purely global property (only checkable once both endpoints are seen), so there is no possible 'shallow structural cue' distinct from the real computation.
even-pairs.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)
even-pairs.preliminary_verdict: likely well-designed (structurally shortcut-free: global answer, no local cue possible)

parity.structural_note: Cumulative XOR over the whole string; global property, no local shape to violate. Negative control: every negative is structurally 'hard' by construction.
parity.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)
parity.preliminary_verdict: likely well-designed (structurally shortcut-free: global answer, no local cue possible)

repeat-01.computes: exact string (01)^n for some n>=0 (strict alternation starting with 0, even length)
repeat-01.structural_note: Extremely rigid grammar (one valid string per even length); local alternation-mismatch is checkable at the first out-of-place bit.
repeat-01.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

first.computes: first symbol is 1 (rest of the string is irrelevant)
first.structural_note: The entire task reduces to reading ONE bit; there is no deeper computation to bypass via a shortcut -- the trivial solution IS the correct solution.
first.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)
first.preliminary_verdict: N/A -- trivial task, no deeper computation to shortcut around

dyck-2-3.computes: balanced bracket string, 2 bracket types, max nesting depth 3
dyck-2-3.structural_note: Stack-based matching; violations (closing an empty stack, wrong closing type, unclosed at EOS) can occur at any position depending on where edits or randomization land.
dyck-2-3.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

majority.structural_note: Global count comparison over the whole string; like parity, no local shape to violate before the end.
majority.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)
majority.preliminary_verdict: likely well-designed (structurally shortcut-free: global answer, no local cue possible)

stack-manipulation.computes: simulate a sequence of PUSH/POP operations on an initial stack; output must equal the reversed final stack contents
stack-manipulation.structural_note: Rich structure (PUSH/POP validity, marker placement, final-stack match); violations can be early (invalid op sequence) or late (correct ops, wrong reported final stack).
stack-manipulation.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)
stack-manipulation.example_hard_negative: # POP 0 POP POP POP 0 # # POP PUSH POP 0 # 1 PUSH POP # PUSH 0 PUSH 1 # 1 PUSH # POP PUSH 0 PUSH

marked-reversal.structural_note: Marker + transform family: violation is early if marker count/position is wrong, late if the suffix content itself is wrong.
marked-reversal.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

unmarked-reversal.structural_note: Mirror-position check; violation is only provable once the LATER member of a mismatched (i, n-1-i) pair is reached, which is on average around the back half of the string.
unmarked-reversal.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

marked-copy.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

missing-duplicate-string.computes: w + w with exactly one '1' replaced by a MISSING placeholder
missing-duplicate-string.structural_note: Marker(_)-count family; violation provable at the 2nd '_' occurrence if over-counted, or at the mirror position of a genuine content mismatch.
missing-duplicate-string.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

odds-first.structural_note: Marker + transform family, transform = odd-indexed-then-even-indexed reorder.
odds-first.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

binary-addition.computes: binary x + y = z (LSB-first bit encoding)
binary-addition.structural_note: Operator/equals-count family: extra operators are provable immediately at the 2nd occurrence; a correct-shape-but-wrong-arithmetic z is only provable at the first wrong bit of z, near the end of the string.
binary-addition.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

binary-multiplication.computes: binary x * y = z (LSB-first bit encoding)
binary-multiplication.negative_generation: mix of perturbed-positive (few random edits) and uniform-random strings, rejection-sampled against is_negative() (50/50 nominal proposal rate, see src/recognizers/string_sampling/sample_dataset.py)

compute-sqrt.computes: x = floor(sqrt(x)) (LSB-first bit encoding, one '=' separator)
compute-sqrt.structural_note: Equals-count family: extra '=' provable immediately; wrong z bits provable near the end.
